<!-- generated by scripts/cli-reference.mjs from `goback docs`; do not edit -->

The config lists the store once and each backup with its kind and schedule. Store settings come from
the file; a global flag or its variable overrides one.

```sh
goback [global flags] agent <command>
```

## agent run

run the backups until SIGTERM; SIGHUP reloads the backups

```sh
goback [global flags] agent run [flags]
```

| Flag | Description | Environment | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--config value` | the agent's YAML config file | `GOBACK_CONFIG` |  |

## agent check

validate the config, open the store, print each job's last run and next due time, and list what each database lacks

```sh
goback [global flags] agent check [flags]
```

| Flag | Description | Environment | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--config value` | the agent's YAML config file | `GOBACK_CONFIG` |  |

## agent status

print the status file a running agent writes, without touching the store

```sh
goback [global flags] agent status [flags]
```

| Flag | Description | Environment | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--config value` | the agent's YAML config file | `GOBACK_CONFIG` |  |
| `--check` | exit 1 when the agent is hung or a job is stale, 2 when there is no status to read |  |  |
